items.title: Development of a teacher-delivered, school-based mental health promotion programme for adolescents in China: a Delphi study.
items.authors: Li P, Wu J, Liu X, Luo Y, Tong Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Strengthening social and emotional competencies (SECs) is a promising upstream strategy for adolescent suicide prevention. However, the existing school-based programmes cannot be directly transplanted into the Chinese school environment. It could be attributed to the different psychosocial challenges faced by adolescents, educational structures, and implementation constraints in China. To address this gap, this study developed a culturally adapted, teacher-delivered, school-based mental health promotion programme to enhance adolescents' SECs and support suicide prevention in China.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study involved a needs assessment and pilot implementation to inform the development of a school-based mental health promotion programme. Drawing on these preliminary findings, two rounds of Delphi consultations were conducted to assess the programme. The experts assessed the importance and appropriateness of the core modules and sessions, as well as the feasibility of the standardised session structure and teacher training strategies. In both Delphi rounds, the experts independently rated each item on a five-point Likert scale (1-5) and provided open-ended comments. For each item, consensus was defined as a mean score ≥ 4.0, a coefficient of variation (CV) ≤ 0.25, and an agreement rate of ≥ 80%. A total of 25 experts participated in the evaluation, including psychiatrists and child and adolescent clinical and educational psychologists.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The final programme comprised three parts: core modules and sessions, session structure, and teacher training strategies. The five modules-emotion regulation, interpersonal relationships, self-confidence, resilience, and crisis prevention-consisted of 25 sessions (45 min each). Each session was structured into seven steps: warm-up; theme introduction; boundaries and rules in discussion; scenario presentation; group discussion; summarisation and feedback; and emotional relief, if necessary. The training strategies for teachers consisted of instructive lectures on key points, core modules, and sessions of the proposed programme; demonstration of proposed sessions; on-site supervision of sessions conducted by trained teachers; online discussion and communication; and continued feedback and encouragement.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study developed a teacher-delivered, school-based mental health promotion programme for adolescents in China. The proposed programme is culturally adaptable, has the potential to be integrated into routine school practices, and holds promise for supporting adolescent suicide prevention.

items.title: The Cognitive Functions of Youth With Obesity: A Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Lin YC, Chang CC, Chang YT, Liu WL, Liao YC, Lin RT.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This meta-analysis examined the associations between obesity and performance across seven cognitive domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility, working memory, verbal fluency, planning, attention, and intelligence quotient [IQ]) in youth under 18 years. Developmental stage (school-aged children vs. adolescents) and sample sex composition examined as moderators. Evidence on executive function in youth with comorbid obesity and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) was synthesized qualitatively.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following PRISMA guidelines, 22 studies comparing youth with obesity to normal-weight peers were included. Effect sizes (Hedges' g) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses compared school-aged children and adolescents; meta-regression examined age and proportion of female participants as study-level moderators.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Youth with obesity performed significantly worse than normal-weight peers on inhibition (g^+ = -0.193), cognitive flexibility (g^+ = -0.499), working memory (g^+ = -0.652), verbal fluency (g^+ = -0.420), attention (g^+ = -0.526), and IQ (g^+ = -0.288); planning could not be estimated. School-aged children showed deficits on inhibition, working memory, and attention; adolescents on working memory and attention only. Between-subgroup tests were non-significant for all domains (p ≥ 0.26), so developmental differences should be interpreted with caution. Meta-regression showed that a higher proportion of female participants in a study sample, a study-level characteristic rather than an individual-level effect, was associated with larger working memory deficits (p = 0.002); age did not moderate any domain. Two ADHD-comorbidity studies received qualitative synthesis only.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Obesity is associated with poorer cognitive performance in youth across several domains, with sex composition of the study sample emerging as a moderator of the working memory finding; differences between school-aged children and adolescents were not significant and should be interpreted cautiously. Substantial heterogeneity, predominantly observational designs, inconsistent BMI criteria, and limited ADHD-stratified data constrain causal inference. Future studies should standardize weight definitions, report age- and ADHD-stratified data, and consider bidirectional pathways.

items.title: Gender Differences in Associations Between Problematic Pornography Use and Symptoms of Depression and Anxiety: Insights From a Large-Scale Study.
items.authors: De Luca I, Ciocca G, Corazza O, Esposito G, Tinella L, Koós M, Nagy L, Demetrovics Z, Kraus SW, Potenza MN, International Sex Survey Consortium, Bőthe B.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Problematic pornography use (PPU) has been associated with symptoms of depression and anxiety. These associations have been studied in clinical and adolescent samples, but little attention has been paid to gender differences in international general population samples. This study examined relationships between PPU, anxiety symptoms, and depression symptoms, with a focus on potential gender differences.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Data were obtained from the International Sex Survey (ISS), a large-scale, cross-sectional study conducted across 42 countries. It involved 82,243 participants (Mean_age = 32.39 years, SD = 12.52; 39.6% men, 57.0% women, 3.4% gender diverse). Participants completed validated measures, including the Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale (PPCS) and the Brief Symptom Inventory's (BSI-18) depression and anxiety symptoms subscales. A one-way ANOVA was used to assess gender differences, while regression analysis examined the role of gender (i.e., men, women, and gender-diverse individuals) in the associations between psychological distress (i.e., depression and anxiety symptoms) and PPU.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Men reported the highest PPU levels, whereas gender-diverse participants reported the highest anxiety and depression levels, followed by women. PPU was positively correlated with anxiety and depression symptoms, with small-to-moderate associations ( r  = 0.207 and r  = 0.249, respectively). Gender significantly moderated both associations, with the steepest positive slopes among men, suggesting that they might rely more heavily on pornography as a maladaptive coping mechanism.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study highlights differences between PPU and mental health across gender identities. While gender-diverse individuals experience the highest levels of psychological distress, men demonstrate the strongest link between such distress and PPU. These findings highlight the need for gender-sensitive mental-health interventions addressing PPU and its psychological implications.

items.title: Electroacupuncture May Alleviate Depression and Exerts Anti-Inflammatory Effects Through IDO1 Modulation of the Kynurenine Pathway.
items.authors: Chen B, Wu X, Ying X, Zhang J, Jiang S, Di Z, Chen Y, Huang Y, Chang H, Ma R, Guo Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Depression is one of the most common mental health conditions worldwide. Numerous studies have identified various factors associated with the onset of depression. Among these factors, inflammation is a key contributor. During the inflammatory process, pro-inflammatory cytokines activate indole-2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), which converts tryptophan (TRP) to kynurenine (KYN) via the KYN pathway (KP). This increases the production of neurotoxic byproducts, thereby exacerbating depressive symptoms. Studies have shown that electroacupuncture (EA) has anti-inflammatory and antidepressant properties. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of EA on depression and its mechanisms of action via IDO1 and the KP.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An inflammation-induced depression mouse model was created by injecting lipopolysaccharide (LPS) intraperitoneally. After the model was successfully established, the Hegu (L14) and Taichong (LR3) acupoints were treated with EA at a frequency of 15 Hz and an intensity of 0.3 mA for 45 min. A subset of mice received ketamine as an antidepressant intervention. The following assessments were performed: open-field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT), forced swim test (FST), and tail suspension test (TST). An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure IDO1 levels and related inflammatory factors in brain tissue and peripheral blood. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was used to measure KP metabolism-related metabolite levels. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was used to measure IDO1 and inflammation-related factor levels.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: LPS significantly induced depression-like behavior in mice. Ketamine effectively alleviated this behavior, exerting an antidepressant effect and suppressing IDO1 expression, as well as the levels of inflammatory factors (IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6). Following EA intervention, depression-like behavior in mice with LPS-induced depression was alleviated. EA effectively reduced peripheral and central inflammatory factor expression levels and suppressed IDO1 expression. EA alleviated depressive symptoms in mice by modulating the IDO1-mediated KP.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: EA effectively reduced the expression of inflammatory factors, alleviated LPS-induced depressive-like behavior, and improved depressive symptoms by modulating the IDO1-mediated KP.

items.title: Research Landscape of Chronic Pain and Neuropsychiatric Symptoms (1983-2025): A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis.
items.authors: Quan X, Fu X, Lu T, Lai J, Qiang J, Chen X, Chen S, Zhu R, Zhang M, Niu X.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Chronic pain affects a substantial proportion of the global adult population and is closely associated with neuropsychiatric symptoms, such as depression and anxiety, which may further worsen pain outcomes and increase mortality risk. However, development trends and research hotspots in this field remain insufficiently clarified. This study aimed to provide a macroscopic overview of research on the relationship between chronic pain and neuropsychiatric symptoms and to identify future directions for research and clinical practice, with particular attention to interdisciplinary collaboration and personalized treatment strategies.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 3627 publications between 1983 and 2025 were included in the final analysis. Bibliometric analyses and visualizations were performed using the R-based Bibliometrix package, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Microsoft Excel 2019.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The number of publications in this field showed a steady upward trend, with rapid growth after 2017. Among contributing countries, the United States emerged as the most active contributor and demonstrated the strongest international collaboration. Leading institutions, including Harvard University; high-impact journals, such as Neurology and Headache; and influential researchers, such as Lipton RB, made prominent contributions to the field. Keyword co-occurrence, citation burst, and thematic evolution analyses indicated that "chronic pain," "pain management," "migraine," "depression," and "anxiety" remained central research themes, whereas "long COVID," "mental health," and "quality of life" may represent emerging future research directions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Research in this field is increasingly shifting toward integrated pain management that incorporates neuropsychiatric and psychosocial dimensions. Future academic and clinical efforts should prioritize the development of individualized treatment frameworks to optimize patient outcomes and refine existing pain management protocols.

items.title: INTENSIFY-a randomized, controlled trial to investigate the effect of an early intensified pharmacological treatment for major psychiatric disorders after treatment failure in the current episode: a study protocol.
items.authors: Okhuijsen-Pfeifer C, Serretti A, Vieta E, Ilzarbe L, Fabbri C, Howes O, Schubert KO, Clark SR, Liu D, Hofer A, Gasser S, Hasan A, Strube W, Driessen M, Ratnalingam E, Reif A, Schiweck C, Engelmann J, Englisch S, Fromme SE, Birner RS, Zobel VJ, Weiser M, Amiaz R, Minelli A, Vita A, Manchia M, Paribello P, Mucci A, Bucci P, Rocca P, Brasso C, Craggs M, Stefanis N, Kokras N, Ebner-Priemer U, Fossati P, Ueberberg B, Assion HJ, van Hell HH, van de Ven PM, van den Bor RM, van Boxel RP, Psych-STRATA consortium group, Rossum IW, Baune BT.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Schizophrenia, bipolar depression and major depressive disorders collectively affect over 10 million people across the European Union and are associated with annual healthcare and societal costs of more than 600 billion euros. When diagnosed, patients are usually prescribed psychotropic medication. A substantial proportion of patients insufficiently responds to first- and second-line treatments, which is termed as treatment resistance. While third-line treatments are relatively effective in TR conditions, it remains unclear whether providing these treatments in an earlier phase provides benefits.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: INTENSIFY consists of three international, multicenter, controlled, randomized, open-label trials, with a treatment duration of 6 weeks. After failure of a first-line treatment in the current episode, 1254 participants will be recruited by at least 16 sites and randomized to either a third-line treatment (early intensified pharmacological treatment) or treatment as usual (standard second-line treatment). Adult participants (age ≥ 18yrs) with a diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or schizophreniform disorder, major depressive disorder, or bipolar depression are eligible after a treatment failure in the current episode due to lack of efficacy. The primary objective is to compare change in symptom severity after 6 weeks. The secondary objective is to compare the two treatment arms on changes of severity symptoms, cognitive function, quality of life, functional measures, digital mental health markers, side effects and concomitant medication. ANCOVA analyses will be performed.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Should the current study show clinical evidence that the use of third-line treatment is efficacious and safe earlier to treat severe mental illness, the results could impact treatment guidelines in due course. In addition, the study will contribute to the identification of clinical, digital and blood-based markers that are associated with treatment response to early and intensified treatments.

items.title: Peripheral molecular signatures of major depressive disorder: a systematic review of blood-derived biomarkers for diagnosis, stratification, and treatment response.
items.authors: Jayanth MS, Sindhu G, Murugadoss H, Sadiqbasha MF, Vidya TA, Mookappan S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is biologically heterogeneous, yet diagnosis and treatment selection remain largely symptom-based. Blood-derived molecular biomarkers may offer scalable tools for biomarker discovery, biological stratification, and treatment-response research, but their clinical readiness remains uncertain.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261379864). PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from 2014 to 27 April 2026 for human studies evaluating blood-derived molecular biomarkers in MDD or clinically defined depressive phenotypes with extractable depression-relevant data. Eligible domains included transcriptomics, DNA methylation, non-coding RNA, immune-inflammatory, mitochondrial/metabolic, neurotrophic/neuroendocrine, multi-omics, and machine-learning biomarker studies. Owing to methodological and platform heterogeneity, a structured narrative synthesis was performed rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified QUADOMICS framework, prediction-model studies were additionally assessed using PROBAST, and certainty was judged using a modified GRADE approach.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 9,354 records identified, 25 reports met the eligibility criteria, representing 24 independent participant datasets because two methylation analyses used the same underlying NESDA cohort. Included studies used whole blood, PBMCs, leukocytes, monocytes, serum, plasma, and cell-free RNA across diverse molecular platforms. Individual biomarkers were heterogeneous, but recurrent pathway-level signals involved immune-inflammatory and interferon-related pathways, NF-κB signalling, mitochondrial and energy metabolism, DNA methylation and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopmental/synaptic pathways, stress-response signalling, autophagy, and non-coding RNA regulation. Multi-marker and multi-omics panels showed promising apparent diagnostic or treatment-response relevance, but most were internally validated, cohort-specific, or exploratory. Modified GRADE certainty was low to very low across biomarker domains.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Blood-derived molecular signatures in MDD show stronger convergence at the pathway level than at the individual-biomarker level. Current evidence supports hypothesis generation and biological stratification, but no blood-derived biomarker or panel is ready for routine diagnosis or treatment selection.

items.title: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with antidepressants in major depressive disorder: a randomized, double-blind, single-center, sham-controlled trial.
items.authors: Bares M, Klirova M, Hejzlar M, Biackova N, Brunovsky M, Kostylkova L, Novak T.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (DMPFC-rTMS) has shown some evidence of an antidepressant effect. This study aimed to examine the efficacy and safety of DMPFC-rTMS as a combination strategy with concurrently initiated selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) compared with conventional high-frequency left-prefrontal rTMS (HF-rTMS) + SSRI or sham stimulation + SSRI.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this prospective, single-center, six-week, randomized, three-arm, double-blind, sham- and active-comparator-controlled trial, patients with a current episode of major depressive disorder (MDD) were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive either DMPFC-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), HF-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), or sham stimulation, all in combination with a concurrently initiated SSRI. The primary outcome was the change in the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score at week six of the study. The secondary outcomes included changes in subjective assessment; response, remission, and dropout rates; and side effects of both rTMS and antidepressant treatment.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Sixty patients (20 per group) were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean change in the MADRS total score from baseline to week 6 was -14.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI]: -18.3, -10.3) in the DMPFC-rTMS group, -8.2 points (95% CI: -11.7, -4.7) in the HF-rTMS group, and -12.6 points (95% CI: -16.1, -9.0) in the sham group. However, no pairwise comparisons between these groups reached statistical significance. The response/remission rates (DMPFC-rTMS: 35%/20%; HF-rTMS: 30%/15%; sham: 55%/45%) and the dropout rates (45%, 25%, and 25%, respectively) did not differ significantly between the groups. No serious adverse events occurred.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study did not demonstrate superior efficacy of DMPFC-rTMS or HF-rTMS over sham stimulation when initiated concurrently with SSRIs. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory. The trial was underpowered to detect the likely incremental effect of adding rTMS to a concurrently initiated SSRI and was further limited by a high sham response and differential attrition in the DMPFC-rTMS arm. Optimal stimulation parameters and patient selection require further validation.

items.title: Smartphone addiction screening status and associated physical and neuropsychological symptoms among Syrian university students: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Abou Kheir F, Jalal Eldin A, Hmidoush A, Mahfoud A, Alhaj Hosen R, Alsoud M, Barakat M, Zakkar M, Antoun I.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Smartphone addiction (SPA) has emerged as a growing public health concern, especially among university students, due to long usage times and the possibility of being affected both physically and neuropsychologically. With little research on these connections in the literature, this study bridges the gap by examining these associations within a single framework in Syria.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional online survey in Arabic was conducted to determine the prevalence and associations of SPA among Syrian university students, using the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV). Self-reported instruments assessed neck pain, ocular complaints, fatigue, cognitive failures, and ADHD-related symptoms using the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), Neck Disability Index (NDI), Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFS), Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), and Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), respectively. Data were collected via Google Forms from November to December 2025.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 1024 participants, 59% were females, 63.6% were students in the medical field, and 60.6% met the criteria for SPA. After adjustment, SPA was associated with higher odds of dry eye symptoms (aOR = 2.78; 95% CI, 2.08-3.71; p < 0.001), neck pain-related disability (aOR = 1.97; 95% CI, 1.38-2.81; p < 0.001), fatigue (aOR = 4.08; 95% CI, 3.03-5.50; p < 0.001), as well as higher cognitive failure scores (β = 5.95; 95% CI, 4.60-7.31; p < 0.001) and higher likelihood of exceeding ADHD screening cut-off (aOR = 4.30; 95% CI, 3.17-5.82; p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: SPA screening status was associated with a higher burden of physical and neuropsychological symptoms among university students. These cross-sectional associations support public health strategies that promote healthier digital behaviours.

items.title: Determinants of alcohol use disorder among adults in Rolpa Municipality, Nepal: a community-based cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Gharti Magar N, Shrestha G, Kandel B, Badal S, Sah JK, Chiluwal S, Poudyal AK.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a major global public health concern, with wide-ranging physical, psychological and social consequences. Socioeconomic challenges, family dynamics and harmful cultural and behavioural factors might play critical roles in the onset and progression of AUD in rural Nepal, such as Rolpa Municipality. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of AUD and identify its sociodemographic, economic, cultural and behavioural determinants among adults in Rolpa Municipality.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A community-based quantitative cross-sectional study design was carried out among 456 participants residing in Rolpa Municipality. Data were collected through an interview schedule using structured questionnaires. A stratified proportionate simple random sampling technique was used to select the participants. The Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test was used to assess AUD, the Family Adaptability and Cohesion Evaluation Scale III to evaluate family dynamics and a validated financial well-being scale to measure the economic status of the participants. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression were conducted to determine the association of problematic drinking with independent variables.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of problematic drinking was 46.7%, with 22.4% identified as hazardous drinkers and 24.3% as alcohol-dependent. Participants with extreme family types (adjusted OR (AOR)=4.55, 95% CI 1.84 to 11.26, p=0.001) and financial difficulties (AOR=2.47, 95% CI 1.10 to 5.54, p=0.027) were more likely to have problematic drinking. Similarly, participants from households that brewed alcohol (AOR=5.25, 95% CI 2.23 to 12.32, p<0.001) and those with poor self-rated health (AOR=2.44, 95% CI 1.49 to 4.02, p<0.001) were also at higher risk of problematic drinking.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study found a considerable prevalence of AUD in Rolpa Municipality, with nearly half of the respondents classified as problematic drinkers. These findings highlight the significance of addressing family support, socioeconomic stability and awareness and health education programmes in reducing alcohol-related problems in this community.

items.title: Sex differences in symptom-specific brain abnormalities across disease stages in depression.
items.authors: Wang X, Xia Y, Bao J, Bao C, Yan R, Yao Z, Lu Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The incidence and clinical manifestations of major depressive disorder (MDD) differ between sexes. This implies distinct neuropathological mechanisms. This study aimed to investigate sex-specific brain patterns in MDD by stratifying patients according to both sex and disease course.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We recruited 1170 participants (811 MDD patients and 359 healthy controls) who underwent T1-weighted and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. We explored duration-stage-related, sex-specific differences in gray matter (GM), amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF), and structural-functional coupling. We also used the structural covariance network (SCN) to assess morphological connectivity reorganization. Finally, we explored the relationship between key brain measures derived from the preceding multimodal analyses and clinical features.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: GM abnormalities in both sexes were observed first appeared in areas supporting sensorimotor and interoceptive functions, and later extended to areas involved in cognitive and emotional processing. Critically, we found distinct sex-specific epicentres of pathology. In male patients, the right postcentral gyrus (PoCG) exhibited early GM atrophy and decreased betweenness centrality within the SCN. In female patients, the left inferior temporal gyrus (ITG) showed early GM atrophy, increased degree centrality within the SCN, reduced ALFF values, and a two-stage evolution of structural-functional coupling with a transition lasting 3 years. Clinically, GM volumes of the right PoCG in male patients were negatively associated with insomnia-early, genital symptoms, and weight loss, while in female patients, GM volumes of the left ITG were negatively associated with depressed mood, work and interest, and psychic anxiety.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study shows a sex-specific neuropathological origin in MDD, with the left ITG serving as the core pathological area in females and the right PoCG in males. These conclusions not only advance our insight into the sex-dependent mechanisms underlying MDD but also provide a stage-informed framework for individualized interventions, suggesting that the early years of the disease may be a critical period for structure-targeted therapies.

items.title: SPARK-ICA: Guided Frequency-Resolved Dynamic Spatial ICA Reveals Fine-Scale fMRI Network Dynamics.
items.authors: Behzadfar N, Iraji A, Calhoun V.

sections.text: Fine-scale spatiotemporal dynamics of functional brain networks are increasingly recognized as critical markers of transient connectivity and neuropsychiatric pathology. However, many existing dynamic fMRI methods primarily focus on temporal variability without explicitly resolving the spatial-frequency content of network dynamics, potentially limiting characterization of subtle, high-frequency spatial reconfigurations. To address this gap, we propose SPARK-ICA (Spatial-frequency Partitioned, Adaptive Reconstruction using Knowledge-guided ICA), a frequency-resolved dynamic spatial independent component analysis (ICA) framework that integrates NeuroMark template guidance with spatial frequency decomposition and group-level ICA of time-resolved, band-specific spatial maps. Starting from template-guided NeuroMark networks, we first estimate time-varying spatial maps using a dynamic guided ICA approach, capturing subject-specific network expression over time. Each dynamic spatial map is then decomposed into multiple spatial frequency bands using Fourier-domain spatial filtering, isolating fine- to coarse-scale spatial features at each time point. Band-specific spatial maps are subsequently concatenated and subjected to a blind group-level multi-frequency ICA, yielding a compact latent representation in which each dynamic component is characterized by distinct spatial-frequency signatures. These group-level band-resolved components are then used as references to estimate subject- and band-specific time courses and maps via spatially constrained ICA, enabling frequency-specific analysis of both long-term correlations and short-term temporal variability while preserving reproducibility across subjects. Using resting-state fMRI data from schizophrenia (SZ) patients and healthy controls (HC), we evaluated both long-term correlations and short-term variability of band-resolved dynamic time courses. For the group-level analyses, we focused on a predefined subset of NeuroMark networks with well-established involvement in SZ-related dysconnectivity. Our results reveal frequency-specific abnormalities in SZ, with enhanced long-term connectivity within sensory and subcortical networks and pronounced short-term alterations involving predominantly higher-frequency spatial components, particularly in cerebellar and subcortical systems. These findings indicate that SZ-related dysregulation is differentially expressed across spatial-frequency and temporal scales, rather than reflecting uniform dysconnectivity. Together, this framework provides a unified approach for analyzing dynamic fMRI networks across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions, extending our previous NeuroMark-DyFICA framework from a predominantly high-frequency spatial representation to an explicitly frequency-resolved characterization of dynamic network organization. By explicitly modeling spatial frequency-dependent dynamics, the proposed method provides a more resolved characterization of network alterations and offers a framework for identifying candidate markers of neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: Transcriptional profiling of antidepressant ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy treatment.
items.authors: Zavaliangos-Petropulu A, Ghang G, Boltz T, Pfeiffer P, Zhan L, Taraku B, Congdon E, Espinoza RT, Narr KL, Ophoff RA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects 30-50% of patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and sub-anesthetic ketamine treatment can relieve TRD, yet their antidepressant mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that peripheral blood gene expression might offer a non-invasive proxy of potential treatment-response biomarkers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a transcriptome analysis on peripheral blood samples from individuals with TRD undergoing ECT (N = 37) or serial ketamine infusions (N = 60), and non-depressed controls (N = 35). Samples were collected at baseline and at multiple follow-up time points. Differential gene expression (DGE) at the single gene and network level identified transcriptional changes and co-regulated gene modules associated with diagnosis, treatment, and response/remission status using Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), correcting for multiple comparisons.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Longitudinal transcriptional changes were not detected for either treatment for individual genes or networks (FDR corrected or |logFC| >0.05). When comparing remitters and non-remitters at baseline in the ketamine group, we observed evidence of enrichment for immune-related functions overall with one gene significantly differentially expressed (i.e., IGKV1-9) (p = 2.5E-05, logFC = -0.51). items.title: Probable Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder Associated With Escitalopram in a Patient With Schizoaffective Disorder: A Case Report.
items.authors: Bin Kamil AlShamsi MK, Ali MZ, Medhat Youssef H.

sections.text: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia in which the normal muscle atonia of REM sleep is lost, and patients act out their dreams. Serotonergic antidepressants such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are a recognized trigger, but in psychiatric patients the nocturnal behaviors are easily attributed to stress or to the primary illness. We report the case of a 46-year-old man with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, maintained on aripiprazole 15 mg daily, who was started on escitalopram 10 mg at bedtime (day one); the dose was reduced to 5 mg on day 77. Around day 430, about 14 months after starting escitalopram and while taking 5 mg, he began to walk in his sleep and act out his dreams, including punching movements and, on one occasion, walking while holding a clothing iron, with no recollection on waking. The episodes occurred late in the night, with his eyes closed, two to three times a month and were accompanied by sleep paralysis and daytime sleepiness. His mental status examination and routine blood tests were unremarkable. He declined polysomnography and brain imaging, so a diagnosis of probable RBD, possibly associated with escitalopram, was made on clinical grounds; a non-REM parasomnia could not be excluded. On day 616, escitalopram was stopped and clonazepam 0.5 mg at bedtime was started at the same time. The episodes had stopped by day 665. Clonazepam was discontinued on day 772, and at the latest follow-up on day 1962 there had been no recurrence. Because clonazepam was started when escitalopram was withdrawn, the improvement cannot be attributed to stopping escitalopram alone, although the absence of recurrence after clonazepam was discontinued supports a role for the antidepressant. Clinicians who prescribe serotonergic antidepressants should take a sleep history from patients and their bed partners, arrange polysomnography where it is available, and review the suspected drug.

items.title: Effect of Maternal Probiotic Supplementation During Breastfeeding on Postpartum Depression and Bilirubin Levels in Low-Birth-Weight (1000-2000 G) Infants: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.authors: Alikamali M, Shahnazi M, Mirghafourvand M, Mostafa-Gharehbaghi M, Homayouni-Rad A, Fardiazar Z, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Evidence on the effects of maternal probiotic supplementation on postpartum mental health and neonatal outcomes in low birth weight infants remains limited. This study examined whether postpartum maternal oral supplementation with Lactobacillus paracasei 431 and Bifidobacterium lactis BB-12 (1×10⁹ CFU/day each) alleviates postpartum depression (PPD) symptoms and reduces total serum bilirubin (TSB) levels in infants weighing 1000-2000 g at birth (two primary outcomes).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, women who had delivered within 48 hours and intended to breastfeed their infants received either probiotics or placebo for 42-45 days. Mothers-not infants-were the unit of randomization (stratified by twin status and birth-weight category). Postpartum depression was assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale at baseline and at 42-45 days postpartum. TSB was assessed at baseline and on days 4 and 7 of the intervention. ANCOVA and repeated measures ANOVA, adjusted for baseline values and the stratification factors were used to compare the groups in terms of PPD score and TSB levels, respectively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: One hundred twenty-two mothers (138 infants, including 16 sets of twins) were enrolled and randomized into two groups. After one mother dropped per group, data from 60 mothers and 69 infants in each group were analyzed. Depression scores did not differ significantly between the probiotic and placebo groups (adjusted mean difference -1.6; 95% confidence interval [CI] -3.9 to 0.69). Similarly, infant TSB levels across days 4 and 7 of the intervention showed no significant differences (0.21; 95% CI: -0.31 to 0.73). One infant death and two cases of positive blood culture occurred in each group.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The maternal probiotic supplementation during breastfeeding in mothers of infants weighing 1000-2000 g at birth did not significantly affect postpartum depression or infant TSB levels. Any potential benefit of higher probiotic doses or longer intervention periods remains speculative and should be weighed against neonatal safety considerations.

items.title: Effect of Midwifery Students' Continuity of Care on Childbirth Fear and Postpartum Depression: An Individually Randomized Two-Arm Superiority Trial.
items.authors: Jafari E, Mirghafourvand M, Abbasalizadeh S, Meedya S, Doshmangir L, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Midwifery continuity of care may improve maternal mental health. Integrating this model into midwifery education may facilitate broader adoption; however, no trials examined its effects on maternal health. We aimed to assess the effect of a midwifery student's continuity of care program on fear of childbirth and postpartum depression (primary outcomes).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this trial, low-risk women at 26-29 weeks of gestation were recruited from Tabriz health centers from November 2022 to February 2023 and assigned to intervention or control groups using stratified block randomization. Twenty-five final-year midwifery students provided continuity of care (each for one to two women) from pregnancy through postpartum for the intervention group; both groups received usual care. Childbirth fear and depression were assessed using the Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale at baseline, and 40-50 days postpartum. Analysis of covariance, adjusted for baseline values, parity, and intended hospital type, was used to compare the groups.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: All 93 recruited women were analyzed; 50% were primiparous. In the intervention group (n=45), 76% attended≥6 antenatal sessions, and 64% participated in≥3 postpartum sessions provided by the students. The intervention group showed lower mean total fear of childbirth (35.8 vs. 75.8, adjusted mean difference (AMD) -43.2; 95% CI: -52.7 to -33.7) and depression scores (5.3 vs. 11.2, AMD -5.9; 95% CI: -8.1 to -3.7) than controls.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The findings support further evaluation and implementation research. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously considering the single-city design, lack of blinding, and reliance on self-reported outcomes.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials, IRCT20100414003706N41, registered prospectively on 30 April 2022, https://www.irct.ir/search/result?query = IRCT20100414003706N41.

items.title: Exploring consumer and carer experiences of a therapeutic group yoga program for eating disorder recovery: a qualitative pilot study.
items.authors: O'Brien J, Evans S, Hoon E, Birch S, Mazza C, McIver S, Pepin G, Harris J, O'Shea M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Eating disorders remain complex and costly conditions, and while evidence-based treatments address behavioural and weight-related symptoms, they often neglect embodied aspects of recovery. This study examined consumer and carer experiences of an 8-week Yoga for Eating Disorder Recovery intervention (YEDRi) offered within a regional eating disorder service.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A constructivist realist qualitative design was used to recruit twelve consumer-carer pairs (mean age = 17 years); ten completed the program and undertook post-program semi-structured interviews. Template Analysis guided iterative coding, stakeholder templates, and team consensus.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Four themes characterised participant experiences. Getting to the Mat showed mixed motivations and early hesitations. On the Mat revealed physical, psychological, and relational benefits. Off the Mat demonstrated how yoga practices supported daily regulation and strengthened family connection. Beyond the Mat identified safety-enhancing features and practical recommendations for future programs.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Therapeutic yoga was experienced as a safe and valuable adjunct to treatment, offering benefits in emotional regulation, embodied awareness, and family connection. Carer-inclusive yoga programs show promise within eating disorder care and merit further investigation across settings and stages of recovery.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: The trial was registered through the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR) (trial ID: ACTRN12625000274471).

items.title: More than translation: an exploratory case study of culturally-responsive modifications in digital mental health for multilingual families.
items.authors: Bobadilla G, Quezada N, Gustafson EL, Stiles-Shields C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Approximately 68 million people in the U.S. speak a language other than English at home. Multilingual families face many barriers to accessing mental health care, including language and cultural differences. Digital low-intensity treatments (D-LITs) can potentially address these barriers by providing accessible, scalable interventions. However, D-LITs must be modified to account for the daily, real-world complexities of youth and implementation contexts. The current case study aimed to systematically describe modifications, informed by feedback from key players, to a monolingual D-LIT to increase access to evidence-based interventions for multilingual families (i.e., Spanish/English).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The Teen Assess, Check, and Heal (TeACH) System is a D-LIT for teens with anxiety implemented via a randomized controlled trial across multiple pediatric primary care clinics serving patients in Chicago, Illinois, USA. By evaluating participant-facing materials and recruitment procedures during the design and implementation stages, we engaged in an iterative refinement process to improve the TeACH System to better serve youth with Spanish-speaking caregivers. Modifications were retroactively coded to document their context and purpose using the FRAME-IS, a framework for documenting modifications to the implementation strategies of evidence-based interventions.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Forty-two percent (155/366) of the teens who assented opted to include parental permission, and 14.6% indicated that Spanish was their guardian's preferred language. Six key modifications aimed to (1) increase health equity through culturally-appropriate content; (2) improve fidelity to IRB consent procedures when engaging with Spanish-speaking caregivers; (3) increase reach of the TeACH System; and (4) improve feasibility of recruitment in primary care settings. Most of the modifications occurred during the implementation phase (83%) and were unplanned/reactive (66%). Recruitment staff led most (83%) of the decision-making regarding modifications. All modifications were applied across the intervention to improve TeACH's ability to better serve multilingual families.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Culturally-responsive modifications must be made at all stages of design and dissemination to ensure that research participation is equitable, even when an intervention is intended to be delivered in English. Culturally adapted and appropriate D-LITs may serve as a catalyst for enhancing the accessibility and utilization of effective digital tools to address mental health disparities experienced by multilingual families.

items.title: Interdisciplinary approach to the study of neighbourhood social cohesion and health: a new framework based on a scoping review.
items.authors: Callahan O, Kössendrup J, Sauzet O.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: We aimed to synthesise empirical evidence on neighbourhood social cohesion (NSC) to construct an interdisciplinary schematic framework.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: An interdisciplinary scoping review was conducted to identify the factors and outcomes related to NSC drawn from journals in sociology, psychology, public health and urban planning.

sections.heading: Data sources
sections.text: A search of empirical literature was administered using PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO and Scopus for English-language studies.

sections.heading: Eligibility criteria
sections.text: We included all studies that examine the role of NSC as a predictor, mediator or outcome within populations residing in Western countries. Systematic reviews or measurement studies were excluded from this review.

sections.heading: Data extraction and synthesis
sections.text: Study characteristics, factors, outcomes and the role of NSC (eg, predictor, mediator) were extracted from 202 studies. To build the schematic framework, we aggregated all factors and outcomes into broader categories previously established by other frameworks. Connections between any two categories were labelled by whether the authors used a longitudinal design and if they attempted to establish causal evidence using a mediation analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The scoping review identified that NSC functions as a social determinant embedded in environmental, structural and psychosocial processes that can operate throughout the life course, interact with demographic structures and contribute to health trajectories through a network of direct and indirect pathways. Childhood exposure to high NSC was associated with developing stronger social skills and prosocial behaviour into adulthood, while exposure to low NSC increased the risk of developing anxiety, depression and substance use during adolescence. Individual resilience and self-efficacy were found to be a linking psychological mechanism between NSC and mental health.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Our framework identifies NSC as a dynamic determinant of health shaped by reciprocal interactions between individuals and their neighbourhood environments. Advancing this field will require research designs that can capture these feedback processes and inform interventions aimed at reducing neighbourhood health disparities.

items.title: A pilot mixed-methods process evaluation of the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of the Familia Bora parenting program for couples with young children in Mwanza, Tanzania.
items.authors: Jeong J, Lambert VJ, Mayombo CW, Uyehara M, Sangarara G, Joseph J, Louttit M, McCann JK, Joachim D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Through a research-practice partnership, we co-designed Familia Bora, a 15-session father-inclusive parenting intervention delivered weekly to couples in mixed-gender groups to promote responsive caregiving, couples' relationships, caregiver mental health, and gender equity and ultimately improve early child development. The aim of this study was to conduct a mixed-methods process evaluation to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of the Familia Bora pilot and to identify opportunities for strengthening program delivery and implementation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The program was delivered from July to November 2024 to 62 couples with a child under 2 years across six communities in Ilemela District, Mwanza, Tanzania. Feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness were assessed using multiple data sources: 90 session attendance records, 75 structured session observations, 79 facilitator feedback forms, 167 participant exit interviews (68 mothers and 99 fathers), endline surveys with 58 fathers, and 37 qualitative interviews at midline and 47 at endline with a purposively selected subsample of mothers, fathers, and group leaders. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data were analyzed using thematic content analysis. Findings were triangulated across data sources to provide a comprehensive assessment of program implementation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The program was feasible to deliver and highly acceptable to both fathers and mothers. Attendance rates were satisfactory among both mothers and fathers. The majority of participants rated the program positively, highlighting its content relevance, cultural appropriateness, and perceived benefits. Sessions on responsive caregiving, economic strengthening, and mental health were rated most favorably, whereas topics like non-violent discipline and fathers' engagement in household chores met some initial resistance due to gender and cultural norms but became increasingly accepted. Parents valued the mixed-gender group format and interactive materials, noting that these aspects fostered critical reflection and participatory learning. Transport reimbursements were also valued by participants and identified as a key facilitator of attendance.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Familia Bora was feasible, acceptable, and well received by both mothers and fathers in this pilot. Findings highlight the promise of co-designed, gender-transformative, couples-based parenting programs for reducing barriers, promoting gender-equitable program participation, and fostering supportive caregiving environments for child development. These results support further testing of this program through a larger implementation study in Tanzania.

items.title: Medical resource use by Team USA at the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games: an observational study.
items.authors: Vincent HK, Oeding JF, Post EG, Triplett AN, Donaldson A, Bartley J, Finnoff JT.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To quantify medical resource utilisation among Team USA during the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games, by illness and injury status.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This was an epidemiological study of athletes who sought care in the medical clinics in the Athlete Village (n=206). sections.text: 1702 clinical encounters were documented. INJ, ILL and had greater clinic visit numbers per athlete (9.6±7.7, 8.5±8.6 and 7.4±7.2 visits, respectively; p=0.049), with maintenance/massage accounting for most encounters. items.title: Association between household crowding at birth and mental health outcomes in school-aged children: retrospective analysis of data from the Born in Bradford cohort, UK.
items.authors: Klaptocz J, Blake HA, Krenz K, Knamiller C, McEachan RR, Ucci M, Sheringham J.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Previous research suggests household crowding is associated with poorer child mental health, but findings are inconsistent. Longitudinal data is required, especially from deprived settings where crowding is most prevalent and in ethnically diverse UK settings where living in larger family units is more commonplace. It is uncertain whether features of nearby green space may modify associations between crowding and child mental health.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analysed data from 3543 children in the Born in Bradford study, a longitudinal cohort representing residents of the ethnically diverse and relatively deprived city of Bradford, UK. We used ordinal logistic regression to investigate the association between exposure to household crowding (self-reported people per bedroom) at birth and child mental health score (normal, borderline, raised) 7-14 years later according to parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), adjusting for gender, ethnicity and socio-economic position. We explored effect modification by ethnicity and green space measures.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Greater levels of household crowding at birth were not associated with being in a higher SDQ category 7-14 years later; in crude and adjusted analyses, the fully adjusted OR was 0.89, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.05. No effect modification by the main ethnic groups or parental satisfaction with surrounding green space at the time of outcome measurement was observed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The relationship between household crowding and child mental health is complex. In this study of an ethnically diverse population, where crowding was relatively prevalent, no relationship was found. Household composition, age, housing condition and family and community support likely play important roles.

items.title: Clinical features and long-term outcomes of anti-DPPX autoimmune encephalitis: a multicentre retrospective study in a Chinese cohort.
items.authors: Chen F, Yu W, Peng J, Xue T, Ma T, Li H, Xie C, Liu H, Wang K, Hao Y.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To explore the clinical characteristics and long-term prognostic factors of anti-Dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6 (DPPX) antibody encephalitis in Chinese patients.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: This study retrospectively included anti-DPPX antibody encephalitis patients diagnosed at three medical centres from January 2019 to May 2024. modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and Clinical Assessment Scale in Autoimmune Encephalitis (CASE) were used to evaluate baseline, short-term (3 months) and long-term (12 months) outcomes. Furthermore, we analysed the relationship between clinical characteristics, immune markers and prognosis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 15 patients were included (median age 45, 60% female). Predominant symptoms were cognitive impairment (66.7%, 10/15), seizures (53.3%, 8/15) and psychiatric symptoms (53.3%, 8/15), with a low incidence of preceding weight loss (6.7%, 1/15); 60.0% (9/15) of patients had abnormal brain MRI findings. Both mRS and CASE scores significantly improved at 3 and 12 months of follow-up (all p<0.05), but 46.2% (5/11) of patients still had memory impairment after 12 months of follow-up. Short-term disease severity (3M-CASE) was significantly positively correlated with hospital stay (β=0.22, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.42, p=0.03), psychiatric disorders (β=2.71, 95% CI 0.26 to 5.17, p=0.03), intensive care unit admission (β=4.11, 95% CI 2.07 to 6.15, p=0.001) and MRI abnormalities (β=3.13, 95% CI 0.73 to 5.52, p=0.02). Long-term disease severity (12M-CASE) was significantly correlated with sleep disorders (β=2.72, 95% CI 0.36 to 5.08, p=0.03). No specific immunological biomarkers remained significantly correlated with CASE scores after adjustment for multiple comparisons. No clinical relapse was observed in the 11 patients with available long-term follow-up data.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study delineates the clinical phenotype of anti-DPPX encephalitis in China. Immunotherapy was significantly associated with improvements in short-term and long-term outcomes. Prognostic factors and relevant immune biomarkers differ between disease stages, underscoring the need for long-term management and stage-specific immunointervention.

items.title: Mental health needs of migrants and strategies to address them: a qualitative, participatory study applying a socio-ecological framework in Barcelona, Spain.
items.authors: Evangelidou S, Giménez L, Muñoz E, Ivars B, Nadal Diaz S, Fusté Vidal M, Pinazo MJ, Requena-Méndez A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Mental health among migrants represents a significant public health issue. The study aimed to explore the mental health needs and mental healthcare access barriers among migrants in Barcelona (Spain) and to co-design culturally sensitive strategies to address these challenges.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study (Sept 2021-Feb 2023) has a qualitative design with reflexive thematic analysis, including adult migrants born outside the EU, North America and Oceania. First, we conducted three focus group discussions (FGD) with 21 migrant women and two FGDs with 12 migrant men (phase 1), and later, three FGDs with 19 professionals working with migrants, including migrant cultural mediators (phase 2). Thereafter, three LivingLab participatory workshops (n=24) took place in order to validate the qualitative results while encouraging the proposition of solutions to improve migrant mental healthcare (phase 3).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A socio-ecological analysis of the qualitative findings was applied. The findings were categorised into five themes: risk factors, mental health conditions, help-seeking behaviours, barriers to mental healthcare access and actionable solutions, each analysed through a single, consistently applied socio-ecological lens across four levels (individual, family, community and structural). The individual level was understood not as the locus of deficit but as the site of embodiment, where family-level, community-level and structural-level determinants are registered. In participants' accounts, distress was seldom framed around discrete pre-migration traumatic events; it was articulated instead through the chronic, everyday conditions of post-migration life, such as precarity, family separation and exclusion. At the structural level, the absence of migrant-sensitive assessment protocols produced a 'diagnostic invisibility', whereby clinically evident distress went systematically under-recognised. Participants co-designed multilevel actionable solutions spanning self-care, empowerment of informal community initiatives, peer-support systems, intercultural initiatives with host communities, cultural mediation and integrative mental health protocols across the social and health sectors.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Holding migrants' lived experiences alongside the perspectives of first-line professionals, participatory processes translated these social patterns into a feasible agenda for action, a concrete move from documenting inequity to acting on it.

items.title: Patient-centred workload clustering in adults under 65 with long-term conditions from longitudinal primary care data.
items.authors: Delord M, Holland E, Shiranirad M, Dregan A, Fraser SDS.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Although patient workload is increasingly recognised as a relevant dimension of the patient experience, it is not satisfactorily captured in current electronic health records. We set out to describe the distribution of patient workload patterns across long-term conditions and demographic groups using electronic health records annotated to reflect patient-centred workload derived from a qualitative evidence synthesis of patient experience.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We used a predefined compendium of 63 workload indicators, derived from a previously published qualitative evidence synthesis of patient experience and mapped to electronic health record codes, classified into eight themes. We computed counts of these indicators in 765 930 patients born between 1956 and 1965 with two or more recorded long-term conditions, randomly sampled from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink. We then used an unsupervised learning approach to construct a typology of patients based on these counts.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Median age at first record was 31 years with 28 years of follow-up. The cohort was 49.4% (n=378 154) male and predominantly white (68.1%, n=521 859). Patients had a median of 15 workload indicators and 4 long-term conditions. Nine clusters were identified, with marked contrasts in workload intensity, long-term conditions, demographic profiles and size. While large clusters were less burdensome, smaller clusters showed more complex profiles, characterised by cardiometabolic or mental health long-term conditions, higher female-to-male ratios and greater ethnic diversity. The most burdensome cluster, characterised by a broad spectrum of rarer long-term conditions and dominated by indicators associated with investigation and treatment monitoring, appeared comparatively less complex.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This unsupervised approach to patient workload revealed patient clusters with marked disparities in burden, long-term conditions, demographic characteristics and complexity, supporting future research directions aimed at better understanding and supporting patients with elevated workload demands.

items.title: From Hospital to Community: Perspectives on Forensic Pathways for Adults With Intellectual Disabilities.
items.authors: Haines-Delmont A, Fradley K, McLoughlin F, Ali S, Raja S, Thomson M.
items.journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adults with intellectual disabilities and forensic histories often experience prolonged hospital stays and delayed discharge, yet evidence on how forensic pathways support safe and timely transition to the community remains limited.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A qualitative, multi-perspective study was conducted within a large healthcare organisation in England. Semi-structured interviews and focus groups were undertaken with service users (n = 11), family members/carers (n = 5), and multidisciplinary staff (n = 18), alongside two co-production workshops with 92 professionals. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Discharge was experienced as a cyclical and unstable process rather than a linear event. Three interrelated themes emerged: (1) establishing readiness and foundations for continuity, (2) maintaining coordination and coherence across the care trajectory, and (3) sustaining community living while preventing re-entry into institutional care.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Supporting safe and sustainable discharge requires continuity-focused integrated pathways beginning at admission and extending beyond discharge to reduce repeated cycles of admission.

items.title: Negative Parenting and Negative Academic Emotions Among Vocational High School Students: A Moderated Mediation Model.
items.authors: Du W, Wang C, Wang L, Jiao D.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Negative academic emotions are significantly associated with the academic achievement and mental health of vocational high school students. The family environment plays a critical role, yet the mechanisms through which specific parenting practices influence these emotions require further clarification. This study aimed to investigate the mediating role of Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) in the relationship between negative parenting and negative academic emotions, and the moderating role of peer attachment.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using a convenience sampling method, total of 1384 vocational high school students from Hebei Province, China participated in this cross-sectional study; questionnaires were administered to students in their intact classes. The study used the following instruments: the Negative Parenting subscale from the Questionnaire of Parenting Style, the Internet Gaming Disorder Diagnostic Criteria Scale, the Peer Attachment subscale of the Inventory of Parent and Peer Attachment, and the Academic Emotions Questionnaire.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After controlling for gender, negative parenting was positively correlated with both IGD and negative academic emotions, and negatively correlated with peer attachment. IGD was positively correlated with negative academic emotions and negatively correlated with peer attachment. Peer attachment was negatively correlated with negative academic emotions. IGD partially mediated the relationship between negative parenting and negative academic emotions (ab = 0.15, BootSE = 0.01, 95% BootCI [0.12, 0.17], accounting for 29.9% of the total effect). Furthermore, peer attachment moderated the first half of this mediation pathway, specifically weakening the positive relationship between negative parenting and IGD (β = -0.08, 95% CI [-0.13, -0.02]).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Negative parenting is associated with negative academic emotions both directly and indirectly through the elevated IGD levels. Peer attachment functions as a protective factor, buffering the adverse impact of negative parenting on IGD. These findings underscore the importance for parents to adopt positive parenting practices and for schools to foster supportive peer relationships to mitigate IGD and alleviate negative academic emotions among vocational students.
